"The Present State of Existential Interventions Within Palliative Care"
searches.purpose: Locate a distinct open empirical review without importing humanistic psychology or positive psychology sources. Selected Terao and Satoh 2022, a CC BY PubMed Central review of 19 randomized trials across nine existential interventions for advanced-cancer and palliative-care populations. Its narrow clinical scope is explicit and it is not treated as a general verdict on existential psychology.

items.title: Existential Therapies: A Meta-Analysis of Their Effects on Psychological Outcomes
items.rights_note: Excluded on rights grounds. The university-hosted publisher PDF carries the notice "This article is intended solely for the personal use of the individual user and is not to be disseminated broadly." Consistent with this corpus's precedent for personal-use printouts, the retrieved body was deleted and is not cached; the DOI and PMID are kept as citation pointers only. This record is not treated as full text.

items.title: The Present State of Existential Interventions Within Palliative Care
items.rights_note: Open full text via PubMed Central under the Creative Commons Attribution License (CC BY). The review covers 19 randomized trials across nine existential psychotherapies for advanced-cancer and palliative-care populations. This narrow clinical evidence does not establish the empirical status of existential psychology as a whole, does not generalize beyond palliative populations, and is not evidence for humanistic therapy or positive psychology generally.
